name: image-cropper
title: Image cropper
description: Choose the crop of a photo: drag it under a fixed frame, zoom with a slider or the keys, lock an aspect ratio and get the rectangle back.
docs: The frame keeps the shape you chose and stays in the middle; the picture moves under it. Drag the picture, zoom with the slider, the plus and minus buttons or keys, a two-finger pinch or Ctrl and the wheel (a notch zooms by about a third); what is outside the frame is dimmed. onValueChange reports { x, y, width, height, zoom } with the rectangle in the picture's own pixels (rounded to two decimals; round before a server cuts with them) and zoom 1 meaning the largest crop of that shape, 2 half as wide. value and defaultValue control it; value null means none yet and the cropper reports the centred one. It also reports once when the picture has loaded and whenever a change of aspect or shape makes a new crop, keeping the middle and the zoom. aspect is a number (1, 4 / 3, 16 / 9) or free, which shows handles on the frame's edges and corners to drag (the frame settles back to fill the stage when the hand lets go); shape round is a circle for avatars. minZoom (at least 1) and maxZoom (default 4) limit the zoom. The frame is the keyboard target and a slider for assistive technology: arrow keys move the crop 1% of the picture (Shift 10%), plus and minus zoom, Home resets, Alt and the arrow keys resize a free frame, and the place is announced as 40% from the left, 25% from the top, zoom 150%. Reset restores the centred fit. A picture that fails to load shows an error with the reason (offline, not an image, or a bad address) and Try again. onReady hands over the loaded image element; cropToBlob(image, crop, { type, quality, maxWidth, shape }), imported from the item's crop module (@rhs-ui/application/image-cropper/crop), cuts the crop out in the browser and returns a Blob (round gives transparent corners, use PNG or WebP). A picture from another site needs crossOrigin anonymous and CORS headers, or the browser refuses the cut. labels carries every word.
